checks.title: Inventory resources have the VantaOwner tag with an owner's email

verify.pass_when_text: Every resource of the types that Vanta inventories (EC2, EBS, RDS, EFS, Auto Scaling groups, S3, DynamoDB, SQS, Lambda, load balancers, EKS, KMS keys, log groups, trails and certificates) has the VantaOwner tag (exact name, with that capitalization) and its value has an email format. A resource without the tag, or with a value that is not an email, fails and one is reported per resource with detail.reason. The Vanta test "Inventory items have active owners" additionally requires the email to belong to an active Vanta user: that can only be seen in Vanta, this check does not verify it. Network resources (VPC, subnets, security groups, NACLs), IAM and RDS clusters (Vanta reads them as instances) are not evaluated. AWS-managed KMS keys (those with an alias/aws/... alias) cannot be tagged: they are not evaluated (N/A); the alias is read with kms:ListAliases. The tags come from the inventory (EC2, RDS, EFS...) and from the Resource Groups Tagging API (get-resources) in each enabled region: S3, DynamoDB, SQS, Lambda, KMS and others are listed without tags. A resource that the Resource Groups Tagging API does not return is treated as having no tags; the service is eventually consistent, so a tag that was just added can take a few minutes to show up. If the auditor role lacks tag:GetResources the check ends up NOT_VERIFIED with that permission.

steps: Decide who owns {resource_id}: a person who is active in Vanta (not a shared mailbox or an offboarded user).
Set the VantaOwner tag with that person's email.
Verify that the tag appears and wait for the next Vanta sync (roughly every hour).
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RESOURCE_ARN="{resource_arn}"
OWNER_EMAIL="__FILL_IN_OWNER_EMAIL__"
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi tag-resources --resource-arn-list "$RESOURCE_ARN" --tags "VantaOwner=$OWNER_EMAIL" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: {resource_arn} is the ARN of resource {resource_id}, taken from the inventory. tag-resources adds or overwrites only the tags given and leaves the rest (S3 put-bucket-tagging replaces all of them). For an S3 bucket use the bucket's region in REGION. No downtime. Vanta only reads the tags, it never writes them. The email must match an active Vanta user: otherwise the resource has no owner even if this check passes. If the team uses another tag name for the owner (for example owner), Vanta allows mapping it to VantaOwner in Settings, but this check looks for VantaOwner. tag-resources reports failures in FailedResourcesMap: review it.

checks.title: The inventory identifies at least one data store with VantaContainsUserData=true (S3, RDS, DynamoDB, SQS)

verify.pass_when_text: Like the Vanta test "Inventory list tracks resources that contain user data": at least one S3 bucket, RDS instance or cluster, DynamoDB table or SQS queue has the tag VantaContainsUserData=true (case-insensitive). If none has it, one account row fails (resource_id account, high severity). Stores without the tag, or with a value that is neither true nor false, are additionally reported one by one, with low severity (detail.reason "unclassified"): they do not break the Vanta test but leave the inventory undecided. Stores with true or false pass. With no data stores in scope the result is N/A (empty), never PASS. The tags come from the inventory (EC2, RDS, EFS...) and from the Resource Groups Tagging API (get-resources) in each enabled region: S3, DynamoDB, SQS, Lambda, KMS and others are listed without tags. A resource that the Resource Groups Tagging API does not return is treated as having no tags; the service is eventually consistent, so a tag that was just added can take a few minutes to show up. If the auditor role lacks tag:GetResources the check ends up NOT_VERIFIED with that permission.

vanta.test: Inventory list tracks resources that contain user data

steps: Decide which data stores hold user or customer data (for the account finding, start with one, for example {resource_id}); for an unclassified one, decide true or false.
Set the VantaContainsUserData tag with that value.
Verify the tag and wait for the next Vanta sync.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RESOURCE_ARN="{resource_arn}"
CONTAINS_USER_DATA="__FILL_IN_TRUE_OR_FALSE__"
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi tag-resources --resource-arn-list "$RESOURCE_ARN" --tags "VantaContainsUserData=$CONTAINS_USER_DATA" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: {resource_arn} is the ARN of resource {resource_id}, taken from the inventory. tag-resources adds or overwrites only the tags given and leaves the rest (S3 put-bucket-tagging replaces all of them). For an S3 bucket use the bucket's region in REGION. No downtime. For the account row ({resource_arn} and {resource_id} do not exist: it is an account-wide finding) pick from the inventory the store that holds user data and use its ARN. Replace __FILL_IN_TRUE_OR_FALSE__ with true or false depending on what the resource holds: do not mark true or false for convenience. Vanta's documentation writes the value ambiguously (True/0, False/1); use true or false in lowercase. To describe what data the resource holds, Vanta also offers VantaUserDataStored (free text), which this check does not require.

checks.title: No resource with a production Environment has VantaNonProd=true

verify.pass_when_text: No resource with the Environment tag equal to prod or production (case-insensitive) has the VantaNonProd tag equal to true (case-insensitive). VantaNonProd=true takes the resource out of all Vanta tests: on a production resource it hides from the auditor exactly what matters most. Resources without Environment, or with another value, are not evaluated and pass. AWS-managed KMS keys (those with an alias/aws/... alias) cannot be tagged: they are not evaluated (N/A); the alias is read with kms:ListAliases. The tags come from the inventory (EC2, RDS, EFS...) and from the Resource Groups Tagging API (get-resources) in each enabled region: S3, DynamoDB, SQS, Lambda, KMS and others are listed without tags. A resource that the Resource Groups Tagging API does not return is treated as having no tags; the service is eventually consistent, so a tag that was just added can take a few minutes to show up. If the auditor role lacks tag:GetResources the check ends up NOT_VERIFIED with that permission.

steps: Confirm with the team that {resource_id} really is a production resource (if it is staging or development, fix the Environment tag).
Remove the VantaNonProd tag, or set it to false, so that the resource goes back into the scope of the Vanta tests.
Review in Vanta the new tests that start to apply to the resource.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RESOURCE_ARN="{resource_arn}"
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi untag-resources --resource-arn-list "$RESOURCE_ARN" --tag-keys VantaNonProd --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: WARNING: untag-resources removes the VantaNonProd tag from the resource and brings it into Vanta's scope; decide that before running the command. {resource_arn} is the ARN of resource {resource_id}, taken from the inventory. tag-resources adds or overwrites only the tags given and leaves the rest (S3 put-bucket-tagging replaces all of them). For an S3 bucket use the bucket's region in REGION. No downtime. However, the resource enters Vanta's scope: red tests that were not evaluated before may appear. If the resource is truly non-production, the fix is the Environment tag, not VantaNonProd. Vanta documents this as scope visible to auditors (they see what was taken out of scope).

checks.title: Inventory resources have the organizational tags (by default Project, Environment and Owner)

verify.pass_when_text: Every resource of the inventory types has each tag in params.keys (by default Project, Environment and Owner) with a non-empty value. One fails per resource and detail.missing lists the missing keys. The keys are configurable in params.keys: neither Drata nor Vanta fixes these names, it is inventory and cost hygiene. AWS-managed KMS keys (those with an alias/aws/... alias) cannot be tagged: they are not evaluated (N/A); the alias is read with kms:ListAliases. The tags come from the inventory (EC2, RDS, EFS...) and from the Resource Groups Tagging API (get-resources) in each enabled region: S3, DynamoDB, SQS, Lambda, KMS and others are listed without tags. A resource that the Resource Groups Tagging API does not return is treated as having no tags; the service is eventually consistent, so a tag that was just added can take a few minutes to show up. If the auditor role lacks tag:GetResources the check ends up NOT_VERIFIED with that permission.

steps: Agree with the team on the values of Project, Environment and Owner for {resource_id} (adapt the commands if the check uses other keys).
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RESOURCE_ARN="{resource_arn}"
PROJECT="__FILL_IN_PROJECT__"
ENVIRONMENT="__FILL_IN_ENVIRONMENT__"
OWNER="__FILL_IN_OWNER__"
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi tag-resources --resource-arn-list "$RESOURCE_ARN" --tags "Project=$PROJECT,Environment=$ENVIRONMENT,Owner=$OWNER" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: {resource_arn} is the ARN of resource {resource_id}, taken from the inventory. tag-resources adds or overwrites only the tags given and leaves the rest (S3 put-bucket-tagging replaces all of them). For an S3 bucket use the bucket's region in REGION. No downtime. Values with commas break the shorthand syntax of --tags: use JSON if needed. Environment should use prod or production in production, because INV-003 and DAT-002 read that value. If params.keys changes, adjust the command to the new keys.
